This is a recommendation for all TV Buyers.

First, the TV is set for Pop and Sizzle, you could say. It's trying to look as impressive as possible, and pretty much every processing feature is turned on. This is good for a store display, but NOT home display.

The thing that everyone should do, as soon as they get their TV in place and working is, research the recommended calibration settings for your TV.

Most will have you flat out turning features off, turning then way down, and even adjusting the color values.

I purchased a 4k years ago and the difference was amazing when you have it set correctly.

Also, everyone should not that pretty much nothing is in 4k, so you're really just going to be viewing 1080/720p content 99% of the time anyway.

For example, take a look at these recommended changes:

https://www.rtings.com/tv/reviews/samsung/nu7300/settings

There's several sites out there that will give you general recommended settings, or exact specific settings for specific models:

https://www.flatpanelshd.com/focus.php?subaction=showfull&id=1439471411

My 4K looks very good, but I have to use the high processing correction mode (which is not energy star compliant because it's doing extensive DSP on each frame), and view in a dark room, then it can look like a movie on 1200 material.

If you get a 4k disk with HDR and your disk matches your player and your player matches your TV, then you get an expanded palette of colors that beats even movie theatres. It's actually pretty great.
